articles.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18.
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
“Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.”
The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a week…

articles.title: Brasil chega a dez milhões de desenvolvedores e ameaça ultrapassar a China no GitHub
articles.summary:
O Brasil chegou a 10,2 milhões de desenvolvedores no GitHub e se consolidou como o quarto país com mais usuários na plataforma de compartilhamento de código da Microsoft. O avanço aproxima o país da China, que soma 12,4 milhões de usuários, e pode levar os brasileiros a ultrapassar os chineses até 2030, segundo projeção do GitHub.
Os dados fazem parte do relatório Octoverse 2026, divulgado nesta quarta-feira (28). Nos últimos 12 meses, 3,28 milhões de brasileiros entraram na plataforma, o dobro do número de novos usuários chineses. Apenas Estados Unidos e Índia registraram mais novos participantes no período.
O Brasil também ocupa a quarta posição mundial em contribuições para repositórios públicos. Essas contribuições incluem os chamados pushes, quando desenvolvedores enviam alterações de código para um projeto.
Segundo o GitHub, o amadurecimento das fintechs brasileiras é um dos fatores que podem impulsionar o crescimento da comunidade de desenvolvedores no país.
IA já participa de boa parte do desenvolvimento de software
O avanço brasileiro ocorre em momento de transformação na programação. O GitHub ultrapassou 225 milhões de desenvolvedores no mundo e registrou 17,9 bilhões de pushes nos últimos 12 meses — volume superior à soma dos números de 2024 e 2025.
Parte desse crescimento está relacionada à adoção de agentes de inteligência artificial (IA), capazes de executar tarefas de desenvolvimento de software.

articles.title: La moda de los dispositivos sin pantalla y por qué cada vez hay más
articles.summary:
La moda de los dispositivos sin pantalla y por qué cada vez hay más
La IA y el cansancio digital impulsan dispositivos que funcionan sin pantalla, sin iconos y, en algunos casos, sin necesidad de sacar el móvil del bolsillo
Durante años, la industria tecnológica parecía obsesionada con una idea: poner una pantalla en cualquier objeto imaginable; y cuanto más grande, mejor. Teléfonos, relojes, electrodomésticos, coches, altavoces e, incluso, frigoríficos se llenaron de superficies repletas de iconos y notificaciones. Sin embargo, en los últimos tiempos ha comenzado a emerger una tendencia aparentemente opuesta: la de los dispositivos que reducen o eliminan por completo la pantalla.
No se trata de un regreso al pasado, sino de una nueva forma de relacionarse con la tecnología. La inteligencia artificial generativa, los asistentes de voz y los sistemas capaces de interpretar lenguaje natural han abierto la puerta a productos que prometen ofrecer información o ejecutar tareas sin necesidad de que el usuario mire constantemente una pantalla.

articles.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with 'Must Eat' feature | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
TikTok has long been a go-to place for discovering new spots, with viral videos helping local restaurants attract new customers. Now, TikTok is making it easier for users to find their next favorite restaurant with a new feature called “Must Eat.”
Introduced Wednesday, the community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform, bringing food recommendations from across the U.S. into one place.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. But instead of relying mainly on search results, maps, and traditional reviews, TikTok is building on what it already does well: connecting people with restaurants through recommendations shared by other users.
“Must Eat” uses more than 40 million posts and comments to pull restaurant recommendations and curated lists together in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and filter results by cuisine, price, rating, and location, making it easier to compare options before heading out.
The recommendations are split into two categories: “Everyday Eats,” featuring casual favorites and neighborhood go-tos, and “Elevated Dining,” highlighting restaurants for celebrations, special occasions, or a night out.
Additionally, select restaurants can be booked directly through TikTok via OpenTable.
The feature is launching first in New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. Users can find it through the search bar, the Local feed, restaurant pages, and location links attached …

articles.title: Un astre jamais vu, situé encore plus loin que Pluton, pourrait rejoindre le très fermé club des cinq planètes naines du Système solaire - Numerama
articles.summary:
Pour l’instant, elle ne porte qu’une désignation provisoire, 2026 ED138, mais elle pourrait à terme rejoindre les cinq planètes naines reconnues par l’Union astronomique internationale (UAI) : Pluton, Makémaké, Cérès, Hauméa et Éris. Cet astre, dont la découverte a été annoncée ce mardi 27 octobre par le Minor Planet Center, l’organisme qui recense les petits corps du Système solaire, est le premier candidat au titre de planète naine repéré par le télescope Vera C. Rubin, mis en service il y a quasiment un an et demi.
Ce type d’astre est trop gros pour être considéré comme un astéroïde et possède une forme sphérique qui le fait ressembler à une planète classique. Contrairement à la Terre, à Mars et aux autres planètes, une planète naine n’a pas fait le ménage sur son orbite : d’autres corps circulent encore sur des trajectoires proches de la sienne. C’est la nuance qui a fait perdre à Pluton son titre de planète au terme de débats houleux au sein de l’Union astronomique internationale, en 2006.

articles.title: Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
articles.summary:
GitHub Staff
GitHub is the world's best developer experience and the only AI-powered platform with security incorporated into every step, so you can innovate with confidence.
See how a record year of growth reached every industry, every field, and every kind of builder in the 2026 Octoverse report.
Developers pushed code to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than in 2024 and 2025 combined.
Behind that number are developers building what interests them and what their communities need. In Nepal, one developer built a flood bulletin on GitHub Pages with verified information on roads, rescue, weather, and power. It has since grown into Gati, a Nepali-first relay of official disaster alerts that runs on GitHub Pages and Actions. Elsewhere, developers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are creating software designed to run programs aboard spacecraft, and fans built open-source firmware that lets people customize their e-readers. Curiosity, aimed in every direction, at a scale GitHub hasn’t seen before.
That growth happened quickly. Partway through the year, activity on GitHub bent sharply upward, just as agents went from something developers were trying out to something they were working alongside. Developers picked from more models than ever and built in industries we are highlighting in this report for the first time, from health care to agriculture.
Octoverse is our chance to step back and look at the whole picture. This year, that picture is bigger than ever…

articles.title: Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
articles.summary:
Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger OLED display this week, and we’ve just gotten to try it out at Apple’s “Pro and tell” event.
Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
We’ve gotten to play around with Apple’s next small tablet.
It’s an iPad for sure, but the new OLED on the Mini looks exceptional, and the optional nano-texture matte finish is awesome. The “Pro and tell” event venue has soft lighting that’s not the most conducive to blinding glare on displays, but the matte finish pretty much squashes it entirely.
Moving the front-facing camera to the long edge is also a welcome change, matching other recent iPad models. (The shift means that the whole iPad line has the camera that way.) The reliance on Touch ID instead of Face ID is still a bummer, though.
The 8th-generation iPad Mini, revealed on Monday, has an 8.5-inch OLED screen, thinner bezels, and a higher peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. The display still tops out at a 60Hz refresh rate instead of hitting 120Hz. It’s equipped with an A20 Pro chip, though the 128GB and 256GB models have five CPU cores, while the 512GB model gets six. Apple has also touted the new iPad Mini’s “Acoustic Display,” which includes woofers “paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume.”
The new iPad Mini starts at $699 and comes in two colors: starlight and midnight. It’s available to preorder now ahead of its launch on November 6th.

articles.title: Can This Vermont Company Remake the Electric Aviation Industry?
articles.summary:
How Beta Technologies Is Clearing the Runway for Electric Flight
It aims to lift the industry with its aircraft, motors, batteries, and charging network
In the cockpit of Beta Technologies’ Alia CX300, pilot Chris Caputo steers onto Runway 33 at Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport in Vermont. Cleared for takeoff, he releases the brakes and nudges the throttle forward.
At the back of the aircraft, the five-blade pusher propeller snaps awake, and the Alia bolts forward. There’s no shriek of a turbofan spooling up, no shudder of a piston engine, and no wait for thrust. Just the low hum of an electric motor and a shove of instant acceleration.
Within a few seconds, we’re at 85 knots (almost 160 kilometers per hour), and Caputo rotates the nose upward. The runway drops abruptly away as we climb. Gaining speed and altitude, we head northwest over Lake Champlain. Through the wraparound canopy, I watch the hunched shoulders of Vermont’s Green Mountains shrink under the right wing, with New York’s taller Adirondacks to the left.
Caputo, a former Air Force fighter pilot, flicks the control stick hard left, then right. Despite its 15-meter wingspan, the Alia feels snappy, its fly-by-wire system automatically coordinating aileron and rudder inputs. The machine, he says, is much simpler to manage than the Cessna 182 I flew around Australia in my student-pilot days.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Node2Shell Exploitation as Honeypots Log Attack Attempts
articles.summary:
The US cybersecurity agency CISA has added the Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. Separately, two security firms say they have recorded exploitation attempts against their honeypots.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and also known as HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell, the flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the decoder of Brotli, the data compression library developed by Google.
It impacts Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. With specially crafted compressed data, an attacker could crash the application, expose the contents of its memory, and potentially execute arbitrary code.
The bug was reported by researchers at OpenAI, and Node.js and Google released fixes on October 21. Microsoft, the maintainers of two Python packages, Bun, Envoy and Istio have also released fixes, and Palo Alto Networks is rolling out hotfixes for PAN-OS.
Imperva has demonstrated that the vulnerability can be exploited for code execution on an official Node.js image.
CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to the KEV catalog on October 27, but provided no information on the attacks. Federal civilian agencies have been instructed to address the flaw by November 10.
Previdian, which monitors exploitation activity through its own network of sensors, says it recorded one exploitation attempt targeting CVE-2026-111497 on October 27, coming from a US-based IP address. The company rates its confidence in the exploitation as ‘confirmed’.

articles.title: The impossible equation of being a researcher mother, striving to make ends meet
articles.summary:
How can we encourage women to pursue scientific careers? In recent years, a number of mentoring or awareness campaigns have been put in place to encourage French high school students to study maths, physics or engineering sciences, while they remain underrepresented in these fields. One of the last large-scale initiatives is the Filles et Maths program, launched in 2025, including work on gender bias, the implementation of “role models” or timetables featuring flexible hours.
The program was nonetheless met with criticism: while women remain under-represented in some disciplines, they also remain a minority in the highest positions across the board in the academic world, from mathematics to social sciences.
In France, gender inequalities are therefore not limited to access to scientific studies: they cut across all university careers and make many women leave French Higher Education and Research before securing tenure. This “drain” is explained by several factors among which motherhood holds an important place. A survey in Denmark illustrates that unlike men, one in three women abandon their scientific career after the birth of their first child.
The survey I have been conducting among doctoral students and social scientists highlights the difficulties faced by women who became mothers before becoming permanent employees. Since the 1980s, recruitment requirements have become tougher with candidates needing to have written a good PhD paper, regularly have their work published,…

articles.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
articles.summary:
Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.
Today at GitHub Universe, we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.
Our vision: From idea to completed software
The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better.
This agentic software delivery system solves for three things:
Velocity: get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible
Intelligence: combine context across the platform with a continuous learning engine, so the system gets better as you use it
Quality: make completed work secure by default and catch bugs before they ship

articles.title: Q&A: Koho’s Daniel Eberhard on unicorns, leadership, and striving to stay humble | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Daniel Eberhard has hit some milestones not many founders have. Last summer, the CEO and founder of Toronto FinTech company Koho saw the company’s valuation reach unicorn status following a $130-million Series E round, joining an increasingly exclusive club of non-AI startups to do so in the post-2023 era.
En route to securing a banking license that, if obtained, will vault Koho into the Canadian challenger bank category, Eberhard sat down with BetaKit Editor-in-Chief Douglas Soltys for a conversation about what he’s learned about leadership on the road from startup to billion-dollar valuation, why he’s not game for prediction markets, and the very peculiar list he keeps in his office. articles.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
articles.summary:
Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility.
AI can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people with different technical skills. The engineer’s role is therefore expanding from performing each technical step to deciding how people, machines, and specialists’ knowledge should work together on the project.
The problem, not the title
Engineering has always been divided into disciplines, and for good reasons. Electrical, mechanical, civil, software, and other engineering fields require deep knowledge that takes years to develop. AI does not replace that need. It simply changes how easily engineers can explore the parts of a problem that sit outside their own specialty.
Consider a software engineer working on a medical device. AI can help the engineer review relevant biomedical research, understand unfamiliar terms, analyze data, and build an early model.

Por eso, la ciencia se centra también en la búsqueda de formas de combinar la luz de muchos telescopios pequeños en una sola señal que los instrumentos puedan manipular. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.

That leaves more FPGA resources for the application. articles.title: Das Ende des Sonnensystems: Wann Jupiter und Saturn aus der Umlaufbahn fliegen

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Astronomen Konstantin Batygin am California Institute of Technology (Caltech) im US-amerikanischen Pasadena kommt nach neuen Analysen jedoch zu einem vollkommen anderen Ergebnis. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen
Bisherige Computermodelle gingen davon aus, dass unsere Sonne ihre äußere Hülle in der Endphase gleichmäßig abstoßen wird, wodurch sich die Umlaufbahnen der äußeren Planeten zwar ausdehnen, aber stabil bleiben. articles.title: Reicht schon ein Macbook mit M1? Diese Hardware brauchst du für lokale KI

Reicht schon ein Macbook mit M1? Diese Hardware brauchst du für lokale KI
Es gibt viele gute Gründe, KI-Modelle herunterzuladen und lokal auf dem eigenen Computer zu betreiben. Ihr behaltet die Hoheit über eure Daten. Nichts wandert in die Cloud eines US‑Anbieters. Weil die Künstliche Intelligenz direkt auf dem Gerät arbeitet, braucht sie schließlich keinen Zugang zum Internet, um zu funktionieren. Und für den vollumfänglichen Zugriff müsst ihr auch kein Abo abschließen.
Je nach Modell kann euch die KI direkt auf dem Speicher wie gewohnt beim Formulieren von Texten, beim Coden oder bei der Bilderstellung zur Seite stehen. Verknüpft man das Modell mit agentenbasierter Software wie Hermes, kann es auch Aufgaben auf dem Computer erledigen, etwa den Download-Ordner aufräumen.
All das klingt gut, ist aber nicht immer ganz trivial. Denn wie gut so ein lokales Modell läuft, hängt entscheidend von der Hardware ab, die euch zur Verfügung steht – oder vom Budget, falls ihr einen Neukauf plant.

Artificial Intelligence
Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
What usually stops PyTorch training from scaling out to a cluster is the container, not the model code. Every container needs the same CUDA runtime, a PyTorch build compiled against it, NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library), the Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) userspace libraries, the AWS OFI NCCL plugin that connects NCCL to EFA, and a Ray version the cluster operator agrees with. Building that image and rebuilding it each time one of those pieces moves is a project of its own, and it has nothing to do with the model you set out to train. The Ray Train Deep Learning Container (DLC) is that image, built by AWS. AWS assembles the stack, tests it as one unit, publishes it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Public and keeps it patched.
Ray runs a job across machines as a single cluster with two roles. The Ray head coordinates and runs the global control store that tracks cluster state, the dashboard and job server you submit jobs to. Ray worker nodes supply the GPUs and run the training processes. Each worker joins the cluster by connecting to the head’s address when it starts. On Kubernetes, each of these is a pod. Kubernetes has no built-in idea of a Ray cluster, so something must create the head and worker pods, start Ray in the right role in each, point the workers at the head, and replace pods that fail. "Artem Stryzhak is a prolific cybercriminal who worked with multiple ransomware groups to target U.S. businesses and hospitals," said Brett Leatherman, the FBI's Cyber Branch Operations Director. "These groups disrupted patient care and caused more than $100 million in losses. Today's sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak's crimes and demonstrates the FBI's global reach and extensive network of international partners."
According to court documents, he paid for 20% of all ransom payments collected for access to custom Nefilim ransomware and decryption keys starting in June 2021.
While active as a Nefilim affiliate until October 2021, Stryzhak used the custom-tailored malware to target large corporations in the United States, Canada, and Australia with revenues exceeding $100 million each year. However, one of the Nefilim administrators later encouraged him to focus on large companies that were generating more than $200 million annually.

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.summary:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

articles.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
articles.summary:
Advanced packaging requires models to cross company boundaries without exposing proprietary processes, but hiding too much can make the prediction break down.
Key Takeaways:
The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain.
For years, engineers moved much of what they needed between companies through datasheets, design rules, and qualification specs, while the manufacturing knowledge stayed with the supplier. That arrangement held as long as the pieces behaved independently, but what one company keeps inside its process now shapes how another company’s part of the package performs once everything is assembled. The process may still belong to the supplier, but its consequences no longer end at the factory gate.
“There’s been some initial work on this challenge, but how do you insert a membrane between the companies so they can share a certain amount of data, but not all,” said Greg Prewitt, director of product management for Exensio Test Operations at PDF Solutions. “Do you obfuscate it? Do you normalize it? How much do you share so both teams can solve a problem without seeing any of the IP that’s proprietary to one company or another?”

articles.title: Cronologia de Zelda: a ordem que a Nintendo só inventou 25 anos depois
articles.summary:
A cronologia de The Legend of Zelda organiza os jogos em três linhas do tempo paralelas que nascem de Ocarina of Time. E aqui vai o detalhe que muita gente não sabe: essa ordem não existia enquanto os jogos eram feitos. Ela foi publicada oficialmente em 2011, no livro Hyrule Historia, quando a franquia já tinha mais de 25 anos e quase 20 títulos lançados.
Ou seja: a Nintendo não escreveu uma saga e depois a dividiu em jogos. Ela fez jogos por 25 anos e depois sentou para encaixar tudo numa linha que fizesse sentido, ou não.
Um jogo de 2011 (Skyward Sword) abre a história. O original de 1986 está lá no fim. Alguns títulos receberam pequenos ajustes de roteiro — retcons — para caberem melhor. E o quadro continua sendo atualizado até hoje: a última mudança aconteceu em setembro de 2026, junto com o anúncio do remake de Ocarina of Time.
Com os 40 anos da franquia e o remake chegando em 5 de novembro de 2026, vale entender como essa bagunça magnífica se organiza.
Preciso jogar Zelda na ordem cronológica?
Não. E essa é talvez uma ótima característica da franquia.
Cada jogo de Zelda é uma história, com começo, meio e fim próprios. Você pode começar por Breath of the Wild, por Ocarina of Time ou pelo remake que chega agora sem ter jogado absolutamente nada antes. O jogo te explica o que você precisa saber.

articles.title: MIT desarrolla software inspirado en origami para lograr construcciones más resistentes
articles.summary:
Investigadores del MIT diseñaron un sistema de construcción modular basado en origami que permite erigir estructuras tridimensionales livianas y extremadamente rígidas sin necesidad de columnas de soporte interior ni equipos pesados de soldadura. El método utiliza bloques de construcción doblados a partir de láminas metálicas planas y un software que traduce diseños arquitectónicos complejos en piezas fáciles de cortar y ensamblar con herramientas manuales básicas.
“Este trabajo demuestra que doblar metal es un método listo para utilizarse en la construcción de estructuras. Podemos hacerlo lo suficientemente grande y resistente como para sacarlo del laboratorio y llevarlo al sitio de obra”, afirmó Neil Gershenfeld, director del Centro de Bits y Átomos del MIT.
El origami tradicional carece de resistencia estructural
El origami en papel es delicado. Hasta ahora, el origami aplicado a la arquitectura tampoco había logrado superar esa fragilidad. Los pliegues convencionales realizados sobre una sola lámina tienden a generar estructuras inestables, incapaces de soportar el peso que exige una construcción real.
El autor principal del estudio, Alfonso Parra Rubio, y su equipo retomaron patrones de teselado desarrollados en la década de 1960 por el artista Ron Resch. En lugar de trabajar con una única lámina de grandes dimensiones y difícil manejo, el equipo del MIT dividió el problema en bloques de construcción individuales más pequeños.

The Browser Choice Alliance (BCA), a group of browser makers advocating fair competition and freedom to choose a browser, commissioned the report, which was produced by the Behavioural Insights Team (BIT).
The report maps any harm to users from Microsoft's PC browser choice practices, focusing on dark patterns that are used by the company.
For those unfamiliar, dark patterns are designs that steer people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make, such as hiding a decline button or making cancellation difficult.
BIT identified 10 dark patterns that it said make it harder to choose a browser other than Edge or subvert a user's choice of an alternative browser after that decision has already been made. These are:
1. Pushing Edge ads when you search for rival browsers: Banners try to talk you out of downloading another browser and steer you back to Edge.
2. Making the switch incomplete: Setting another browser as your default still leaves files like PDFs assigned to Edge, requiring more changes.

articles.title: Nobody Trusts the Security Questionnaire. We Rely on It Anyway.
articles.summary:
Right now, people on security and GRC teams are spending their entire workday answering security questionnaires. At some companies it is a full-time role: a GRC analyst or compliance manager who arrives, opens a laptop, and works through these forms until they go home, two or three hundred of them in a year. I’ve heard the stories. The dinner missed, left a kid’s game at halftime, lost the weekend to a form asking whether the company still keeps tape backups. They do it because the questionnaire sits on the path to revenue. If the form stalls, the deal stalls with it.
There is a double standard built into the process. The same team buried under those questionnaires also sends them out to the company’s own vendors, collects the answers, and files them as proof those vendors are safe to trust. They know how little the answers are worth when they fill them out, because they have watched how little scrutiny the yeses get under deadline. They rely on them anyway when a vendor sends them back, because for a long time there was nothing better to rely on.
The same form, distrusted going out and trusted coming in
Step back and look at the whole exchange. Company A wants to sell to Company B. Before the deal closes, B sends A a questionnaire and a stack of security terms to sign: a security addendum, a data processing agreement, and now an AI addendum. Apple utilise déjà cette technique sur l’iPad Pro depuis mai 2024, et LG Display en a même fait une appellation à part pour ses dalles de moniteurs. L’écran garde ProMotion, le rafraîchissement variable d’Apple. Il monte à 120 Hz pour les contenus les plus dynamiques et descend jusqu’à 10 Hz sur une image ou un contenu fixe, afin d’économiser la batterie.

articles.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
articles.summary:
Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent.
Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
Windows and Xbox revenues have declined during Microsoft’s first quarter of the 2027 financial year.
It’s a new financial year for Microsoft, so the company is changing up how it reports its finances by splitting its businesses into two segments for the first time. Gone are the previous segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It’s now just Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.
Agents and Infra, which includes businesses like Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, and server products, makes up 83 percent ($76.8 billion) of the overall $92.3 billion of Microsoft’s revenue and has increased 25 percent year-over-year. The big changes to Microsoft’s financial reporting also mean we will now see the company disclose Azure revenue on a quarterly basis. Azure contributed $33.17 billion in revenue this quarter, up 48 percent year-over-year.
Devices and Consumer, which includes Windows, Xbox, Surface, and Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses, makes up the remaining 17 percent ($15.5 billion) of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in revenues this quarter — a decrease of three percent.

articles.title: El Niño pourrait provoquer une nouvelle flambée des concentrations de CO2, alerte l'OMM
articles.summary:
La Nasa a prévenu, nous nous dirigeons vraisemblablement vers un épisode d’El Niño « historique » dans l’océan Pacifique. Le phénomène est officiellement de retour depuis l’été, et selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño va se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Cet épisode s’annonce particulièrement intense. Une étude publiée cet été concluait même qu’El Niño est plus puissant qu’à aucun moment depuis 1 000 ans.
Une « nouvelle flambée » des gaz à effet de serre à craindre à cause d’El Niño
Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l’OMM a de nouveau attiré l’attention sur l’impact potentiel de ce phénomène, en lien avec un autre triste record planétaire. « Les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint de nouveaux records, scellant ainsi une hausse des températures à long terme. L’intensification du phénomène El Niño pourrait entraîner une nouvelle flambée de ces concentrations », résume l’organisme des Nations unies sur X.
El Niño est un phénomène climatique naturel. Il se manifeste par des anomalies de températures de surface dans l’océan Pacifique équatorial. Ces températures plus chaudes que la normale peuvent entraîner une cascade d’effets sur la planète. Avec le réchauffement planétaire, ces effets peuvent être encore plus dommageables.

articles.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform.
Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit.

articles.title: AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
articles.summary:
AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
An agent receives approval to process a partial refund. It sends the request to a payment API, and the process crashes. Maybe the payment service completed the refund. Maybe the request never went through. A replacement agent spins up and finds an operation record marked dispatched with no outcome written.
This kind of ambiguity isn’t unique to agents. Any distributed worker crashing mid-mutation faces the same problem. But a conventional worker resumes a predetermined workflow from the last checkpoint. An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own. Given the same customer request and no outcome record, it might come up with a different plan, pick different parameters, or decide to issue a new refund instead of continuing the one already approved.
“An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own.”
If the original refund went through, a second attempt refunds the customer twice. The charge still has enough remaining balance to cover another partial refund, so nothing stops it.
The replacement must inherit the original operation, not reinterpret it.
The operation must outlive the agent
An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not. The refund, its approval, its parameters, its current status. A long-running agent can preserve useful state for as long as it runs. The requirement: no essential operation should depe…

According to Gen Threat Labs, there has been a 54 per cent increase in malicious content served through AI chatbots in the last 90 days.
Separate research has also found more than two-thirds of people are concerned about privacy, data breaches, or losing control of AI assistants that can act on their behalf.
Safe AI is a new set of protections within Norton 360 and can block actions you did not intend and let you decide which personal files AI tools can access and open.
It can also help you avoid risky links.
AI assistants are making things easier for many people, from finding information to getting things done, but that convenience can bring with it new risks.
Safe AI can address these emerging issues and risks and quell people’s concern while increasing Norton’s protection in AI experiences people are using every day.

articles.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the 'For You' feed | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The company announced on Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”
The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.
The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.
Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.
Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed their frustration with the change.

articles.title: Chrome's AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.
That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.
The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.
Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.
As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.
The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

articles.title: What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
articles.summary:
What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
Imagine: There’s a line on the credential report that no one on the platform team can explain. An IAM user called research-agent-2 has an access key created 14 months ago that was last used 11 months ago. And it’s still active.
The project it supported closed long ago, and the person who approved it doesn’t even work at the company anymore.
While this example is hypothetical, the lifecycle problem isn’t.
This doesn’t require carelessness. An agent is created for a task, the task ends, and nobody revisits its access. A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab. AWS IAM user access keys don’t expire automatically, so a forgotten key stays valid until somebody disables or deletes it.
“A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab.”
OWASP puts improper offboarding first in its 2025 Top 10 for non-human identities, and the remedy reads like this series’ premise: retire what’s no longer needed, and give the rest an accountable owner. The hard part is knowing what exists.
The problem is that attackers move faster than an annual audit ever could. In September 2026, GreyNoise documented an AI-orchestrated campaign against PaperCut servers: the attacker went from an empty workspace to remote code execution at a real victim in under four hours, and once launched, the campaign compromised at least eleven organizations in 26 seconds. Enterprises should rethink this idea. Security teams cannot patch at machine speed, but they can reduce what an attacker can reach after exploitation by focusing on identity as the control plane.

Securing AI agents requires continuous verification of actions after login
Modern digital security frameworks were originally built to correct a flawed historical assumption: the belief that if a user or system was inside the company network, they could be trusted implicitly. Over the past decade, the rapid rise of cloud storage, subscription-based business software, and remote working destroyed that network boundary.
In response, our security models shifted focus. We began verifying the identity of the person trying to log in, inspecting the hygiene of their computer, requiring multiple verification steps during login, and continuously checking that they were who they claimed to be.
Chief Information Officer and Global Chief Information Security Officer at Cato Networks.
This model works well when a human is logging in to perform a task. But with the rise of autonomous AI agents, the real security risk no centralized at the login screen. It starts after access has been granted.

As part of the observed attacks, the hackers used the Chinese internet asset search engine FOFA to identify 19,000 internet-facing firewalls from a specific vendor, and proceeded to exploit 25 of them on October 23-24, Dream says.
After discovery, the hackers first filtered servers in the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, then filtered those running newer PHP releases, which gave them a pool of 240 potential targets.

articles.title: Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model

Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
Nvidia on Wednesday launched Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, its latest multilingual transcription model. The new open-weight model, the company says, ranks first on Hugging Face’s Open ASR open model leaderboard for English, with an average word error rate of 5.33%, and also sits at the top of two speaker-attribution benchmarks.
But what’s maybe even more interesting is that this is a promptable transcription model. Being promptable here means that the user can give the model specific instructions before it listens. Typically, that means setting the context for the transcription by telling the model that a given audio file is a medical discussion in English, for example, and giving it a list of medical terms.
Users can also tell the model to label each speaker or ask it questions about the audio. They can request a verbatim transcript or a cleaned-up version, and tell it how to format numbers, for example.
Nvidia bundles these capabilities, along with translation, into a single checkpoint, which could simplify the work of building applications around them.
Ideally, setting this context reduces the error rate. The trade-off is that these models are much larger than traditional transcription models, which are often under a billion parameters in size. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 4 billion active parameters.

articles.title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
articles.summary:
Attackers are actively exploiting vulnerabilities across critical network infrastructure, and PHP flaws known as "PHP2Shell" put the web management interfaces of firewalls, VPNs, application delivery controllers, and other appliances at risk.
The findings come from Eclypsium's October InfraTrust Pulse, a monthly report tracking security advisories affecting network devices, servers, firmware, chips, and other infrastructure.
Between September 18 and October 14, InfraTrust tracked 133 new security advisories across 18 vendors, covering 2,813 vulnerabilities.
Of those advisories, 37 were rated critical, five had a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and 58 could be exploited remotely without authentication.
Sixteen newly published advisories included vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (KEV) as they were actively exploited.
The report also warns that many network appliances, including firewalls, VPN gateways, application delivery controllers, and network-attached storage devices, embed PHP into their management interfaces.
Because vendors compile PHP into appliance firmware, customers commonly cannot install the recent PHP security updates themselves and must instead wait for each vendor to release updated firmware.
InfraTrust therefore recommends that administrators make sure PHP-backed management interfaces are not exposed to the Internet while waiting for PHP2Shell patches.

articles.title: A hidden ocean change near Antarctica could have global consequences
articles.summary:
The rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a dramatic shift in a crucial part of Earth’s climate system, scientists say.
In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in a vast layer of the Southern Ocean, extending from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep and encircling Antarctica. The shift reverses decades of freshening and echoes ocean changes usually associated with major global climate shifts over millennia but is now happening in just a few years.
The switch from a decades-long trend of freshening water to increasing salinity has implications that could extend beyond Antarctica. The layer, known as Antarctic Intermediate Water, spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans, transporting heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics, and even across the equator, said co-author Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and at the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India.
Gayen said the study combined six independent datasets to track changes in the Southern Ocean from 2004 to 2024. The data came from Argo floats, which drift through the ocean and periodically descend to different depths to measure water properties such as density and salinity, then resurface to transmit the readings. A 2025 study also detected increasing surface salinity linked to declining sea ice, he added.

								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: Movellus
								
							
In an AI datacenter, 50 mV of voltage margin can be worth about 270 racks of compute per gigawatt of input electricity. To show how, this paper models two facilities that run the same Vera Rubin NVL72 racks at the same clock speeds, one at 0.80 V and one at 0.75 V. On published Vera Rubin power figures, the second draws about 8% less power per GPU and about 17 kW less per rack.
Margin is the supply voltage added above what the silicon needs to cover the worst-case voltage droop. Evolving AI workloads make that margin larger and harder to predict. As a result, platform and silicon teams often over-margin to compensate, costing them compute density and token throughput, while teams that margin too little see failures in the field.
Power delivery network (PDN) design in the age of AI takes a systematic approach to power management. This paper distills the foundation of that approach into four axioms, drawn from work with customers in AI and high-performance computing (HPC).

Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.

Cybersecurity firm FoxIO has disclosed three vulnerabilities in GoAhead’s handling of TLS. They could keep revoked client certificates working, let eavesdroppers decrypt some traffic, or help attackers get around a cap on certificate chain length.
GoAhead, a lightweight web server made by EmbedThis, runs the management interfaces of networking equipment, printers and industrial systems. According to FoxIO, it is present on hundreds of millions of devices across the IoT, OT, firewall and military sectors.
FoxIO’s Sébastien Féry, who documented the flaws this week, said each one affects only a subset of deployments. Which GoAhead devices are at risk depends on the TLS library the manufacturer built into the firmware and how it configured certificate checks.
The critical flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS score of 9.1), impacts GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 when built with OpenSSL or a compatible library and configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) with a certificate revocation list (CRL). The server reads the list but never tells OpenSSL to consult it.
On these builds, a certificate an administrator has revoked, such as one tied to a stolen or compromised device, is still accepted, even with issuer verification switched on. Nothing at startup warns that revocation checks are inactive.

articles.title: Building an Offline-First AI Coding Tutor for Low-End Android Phones
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- On low-end devices in low-bandwidth markets, a full storage volume is a normal operating condition rather than an edge case, so any await on a cache or database write inside a critical render path is a latent blank screen and should be treated as a non-fatal degradation instead.
- localStorage is the wrong persistence layer for any cache that scales with content or locale, because its roughly 5MB ceiling and synchronous API impose the heaviest cost on precisely the underpowered devices you are trying to serve, while IndexedDB with a dual-read migration window lets you move without stranding existing users.
- WebAssembly runtimes such as Pyodide and sql.js make server-free code execution viable on smartphones, but only if you defer initialisation into a Web Worker and treat cold-start cost as a first-class UX problem rather than a benchmark footnote.
- AI features that depend on a hosted endpoint should be designed with an explicit degradation contract, which includes a defined second tier, a defined timeout, persisted session state across the switch, and feedback formats that stay useful when the weaker model answers.
- Discoverability and usability are different properties, and a feature placed outside a user's working line of sight is functionally a feature that does not exist.

articles.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
articles.summary:
Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon has been using a framework that relies on rotating chains of connected devices compromised on demand, including for zero-day attacks targeting high-value systems.
The framework has been dubbed Silent Train because the threat actor uses it against select targets, cleans it up after each operation, and refreshes it continuously.
Researchers at Black Lotus Labs, the threat research division of communications company Lumen, have been tracking Silent Train for three years and confirmed that Volt Typhoon exploited at least four zero-day vulnerabilities in attacks targeting edge and management infrastructure.
Targets include telecommunication firms, government agencies, defense contractors, educational institutes, utilities/critical infrastructure, satellite service providers, IT firms, MSPs, transportation, aviation, and emergency services.
Black Lotus Labs’ observations indicate the most targeted regions are California, Texas, and Hawaii, suggesting a focus on Indo-Pacific matters.
Volt Typhoon previously targeted U.S. critical infrastructure, including communications, energy, transportation, and water systems, with CISA warning that it seeks to establish access for potential disruption during a future crisis or conflict.
According to the researchers, Silent Train's deployment was partly fueled by the FBI's disruption of KV-Botnet, a botnet that Volt Typhoon used to evade detection when attacking critical infrastructure in the US.…

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.
The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. articles.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
articles.summary:
Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets a browser confirm a visitor owns the email address they typed, without sending a single message. The trial began in Chrome 150 on desktop, with Gmail taking part as the first participating provider.
The idea replaces the familiar one-time code or magic link. Today a user enters an email, leaves for their inbox, copies a code, and returns, a context switch that often loses them. The proposal uses a three-party model where the browser sits between the site (the "verifier") and the mailbox provider (the "issuer"). If the user is already signed in to their provider, the browser quietly fetches a signed token and drops it into the form, and the server validates that token on submission. Google notes the issuer never learns which site made the request.
For developers the front end implementation is fairly straightforward. The email field needs an autocomplete hint, plus a hidden input carrying a session-bound nonce:
<input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="hidden" name="token" nonce={nonce} autocomplete="email-verification-token">
The heavier work sits on the server side, where the token's signature is checked against the provider's keys. Resend's Phil Nash, who wrote a walkthrough of the flow, published an npm package and a Next.js example to handle that parsing and validation.

articles.title: 1 147 pages d'une complexité « redoutable » : les physiciens refusent de publier trop tôt la preuve d'OpenAI malgré l'appel des mathématiciens
articles.summary:
Une preuve scientifique d’une longueur et d’une complexité remarquables. C’est ainsi qu’ont réagi les cinq physiciens à la lecture de la démonstration écrite par un modèle d’intelligence artificielle de la société américaine OpenAI, au sujet de l’un des sept grands problèmes du prix du millénaire : la théorie de Yang-Mills.
OpenAI affirme que son modèle a prouvé l’existence de la théorie quantique de Yang-Mills sur le plan mathématique.
Cette théorie est la base de la chromodynamique quantique, qui décrit l’interaction nucléaire forte. C’est elle qui colle les quarks entre eux. Les quarks sont les briques des protons et des neutrons, au cœur des noyaux atomiques.
Ces cinq scientifiques, sollicités par OpenAI pour analyser les travaux de ce modèle d’IA, ne se prononcent pas à ce stade sur la véracité de la preuve. Dans leur communiqué commun, publié ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, ils se contentent d’en noter les contours : on parle d’un document long de 1 147 pages et d’une technicité manifeste. D’où leur réaction initiale.
« La longueur et la complexité des manuscrits d’OpenAI sont redoutables, et il faudra du temps pour en assimiler la méthodologie et la portée, aussi bien en physique qu’en mathématiques », préviennent-ils. « Notre groupe de travail mènera les efforts pour y parvenir. » À l’issue de ce travail, le groupe prévoit bien de publier la preuve, accompagnée de son analyse.
Vérifier d’abord que la preuve est correcte

Conocido como Gemini 4 Carbon, esta variante cuenta con capacidades de programación y razonamiento avanzado, así como funciones especializadas en ciberseguridad. Según la tecnológica, Carbon es eficaz para encontrar y corregir fallos de seguridad.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su blog, Gemini 4 Carbon toma el relevo de Argon, que se anunció hace apenas unas semanas. Google ya no quiere dejar pasar mucho tiempo entre un lanzamiento y otro, por lo que agilizó los tiempos de desarrollo para cerrar la brecha con Anthropic y OpenAI. Otro factor para el despliegue de este modelo es la oleada de hackeos por parte de agentes autónomos, los cuales vulneraron múltiples empresas y gobiernos en los últimos meses.

Northstar launches with $7M to give AI agents the context to act on security risks
Cybersecurity startup Northstar Security AI Inc. launched today with $7 million in new funding to give artificial intelligence agents the context they need to act on security risks.
Northstar offers a platform that feeds data from a company’s existing security and information technology tools into a real-time Security Context Graph. A known vulnerability, an unmanaged device or an overprivileged account can look manageable on its own.
Put together, the same issues can leave a critical business system exposed. Those toxic combinations are what the graph is meant to find, since the underlying data usually sits in tools that don’t share it.
A company laptop with no endpoint protection is the example Northstar uses to illustrate the problem. Working out whether that one device poses a meaningful risk can mean going through six different tools. An analyst on the platform can type that question in plain language.
In that scenario, the reply shows the laptop belongs to a privileged user who can reach the payroll system. Fixing it then falls to Northstar’s AI agents, which can kick off a remediation workflow to push endpoint protection onto the machine. Humans can supervise those steps where appropriate.

Son doux nom ? CVE-2026-97631. Révélée le 22 octobre 2026, elle se loge dans le firmware de la plupart des serveurs, sous le système d’exploitation, dans des couches logicielles que personne ne voit jamais.
Interrogé par le site américain Ars Technica, HD Moore, directeur de la recherche chez Dragos, une entreprise spécialisée dans la sécurité des infrastructures industrielles, la qualifie déjà de « bug éternel ».

L’attaque se joue dans un laps de temps très réduit, pratiquement à l’instant où notre doigt lâche le bouton d’allumage. Quand on allume un serveur, le système d’exploitation n’est pas le premier programme à se lancer. Avant lui s’exécute le firmware, un logiciel stocké sur une puce de la carte mère, qui vérifie le matériel puis passe la main au système.
Sur les machines modernes, ce firmware suit une norme appelée UEFI. La plupart des fabricants le construisent à partir d’une même base de code open source, EDK2, que les grands fournisseurs du secteur comme AMI, Insyde ou Phoenix utilisent abondamment. Jusque-là, rien de compliqué.
Sauf que dans les centres de données, les serveurs ne démarrent pas toujours depuis leur disque. Pour installer des centaines de machines sans intervenir sur chacune, les administrateurs utilisent le démarrage réseau, ou PXE, qui permet à un serveur de récupérer …

In context: Communities across the US have pushed back against the deployment of AI-powered automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) because of concerns about mass surveillance. Reports over the past year or so illustrate how authorities have used data from these devices to conduct traffic stops based on nothing more than "suspicious" travel patterns.
The ACLU recently outlined a pattern of police traffic stops based solely on data from Flock cameras and other license plate readers. The reports go back to at least 2025 and show how closely authorities can track the movements of most motorists.
In one case from late 2025, a woman only understood the extent of the surveillance when an officer demonstrated the software following a traffic stop. As she traveled through several states on a road trip to Florida, a self-identified FBI agent ran her license plate through a database and stopped her simply because she was from another state and her recent travels seemed unusual compared to the information the ALPR network had on her.
Although the account did not specifically mention Flock, the agent likely used a database built by Flock or another company that has installed ALPRs in thousands of communities nationwide. The AI-powered cameras automatically input passing cars' license plates (not always accurately) into nationwide databases that authorities can search without warrants.

articles.title: Hacker stole personnel data about thousands of Homeland Security employees, including CBP and ICE agents | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.
The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.
A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.
More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.
The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.

articles.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
articles.summary:
If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden’s win that November. If you ask Google’s AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources.
When I put the direct question of “Who won the 2020 presidential election?” to Google’s AI Mode this morning (after seeing complaints about cagey answers on social media), I got the following surprisingly indirect response:
“To review the official results and statistics of the 2020 United States presidential election, including the final electoral college breakdown, popular vote counts, and winner certification, please consult the official report compiled by the Federal Election Commission (FEC).”
My testing resulted in a similarly indirect answer when asking about the 2024 presidential election, with Google’s AI telling me to just consult the FEC for that information. Asking about 2012 election resulted in a link to The American Presidency Project’s 2012 Data Center rather than a direct answer. But AI Mode seemed perfectly willing to give me a detailed and correct responses for the winner of every other presidential election going back to 2000.

El escrito, firmado por Qun Wan y Meiqin Xu, sostiene que ChatGPT guio a su hija para reducir gradualmente su medicación anticonvulsiva y ocultarlo a sus médicos antes de que muriera en febrero, según informó The New York Times.

A Anatel tornou obrigatória a validação biométrica para ativar e manter linhas de celular. A nova regra, aprovada pela Superintendência de Planejamento e Regulamentação e divulgada nesta quarta-feira (28/10), vale para pessoas físicas e microempreendedores individuais (MEI) e será implantada gradualmente até o fim de 2028.

O objetivo é dificultar a abertura e a transferência de linhas usando dados falsos ou de terceiros. Uma das fraudes mais conhecidas é o SIM swap, em que criminosos conseguem transferir o número da vítima para outro chip e passam a receber ligações e códigos de autenticação enviados por SMS.

Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language
Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.

Pourquoi le tribunal a-t-il infligé à Marie-Line X une amende de 500 euros ? Tout d’abord, la contribuable bretonne avait déjà déposé une requête similaire, qui avait été rejetée. Ensuite, elle a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes sans avoir préalablement adressé de réclamation à l’administration fiscale, une démarche obligatoire dans ce type de litige. articles.title: Smart TVs spy on you, even when you opt out: study
articles.summary:
A new study has shown that your smart TV might be tracking you and what you watch, even when you opt out of tracking.
The study, named Watching the Watchers, was conducted by researchers affiliated with Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts.
- Essentially, it examines automatic content recognition (ACR) features, which the study noted are built into most available smart TVs—and whether turning ACR off actually stops TVs from sending whatever is on your screen to providers.
The researchers tested TVs running Tizen OS (Samsung), Roku OS (Roku, TCL), webOS (LG), SmartCast OS (Vizio), Google TV OS (Sony, Hisense, TCL), Fire TV OS, and others like VIDAA and Xumo.
To add some context, here is how ACR works: essentially, the TV takes short audio or video snapshots of what is on screen, and those snapshots (or the digital fingerprints made from them) are then sent to the internet or ACR provider. From there, the provider compares what was sent to a library of known content to determine exactly what you are watching. The data can reveal your viewing habits and can be used for targeted ads or sold to other companies.
Interestingly, the researchers found out that antenna broadcasts were almost always tracked on every analyzed system. On the streaming side, no TV tracked YouTube or Netflix, but free ad-supported streaming platform Tubi was tracked on Tizen OS, Google TV on Sony, and VIDAA OS.
The researchers also noted that most operating systems tracked their own streaming se…

articles.title: This open-source keyboard lets you snap keys together in any layout
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Custom keyboard builders can swap out switches, keycaps, plates, and firmware these days, but the layout is usually locked in once the PCB is made. Now, a new open-source project called Keybytes is trying to get around that limitation by giving each key its own tiny circuit board and microcontroller. The keys snap together with magnets and connect to a small hub, allowing a keyboard to start out as a single key and grow into pretty much any shape.
The project comes from Nathan Alspaugh, an MIT freshman studying aerospace engineering, who said he has spent around 100 hours working on it since March. When he posted the project to Hacker News this week, he said the idea came from his frustration that nobody sold triangle- or circle-shaped keyboards.
Each key, called a Keybit, consists of a 19.05mm-square circuit board fitted with a Cherry MX switch and an inexpensive CH32V003 RISC-V chip. The neighboring module, whether another key or the hub, receives power and I2C data through spring-loaded pogo pins along all four edges.
The hub, called the Keyword, occupies the same 1u footprint but stacks two PCBs. An STM32WB55 on the upper board handles Bluetooth and stores firmware for every key. Meanwhile, the lower board houses the charging circuitry for an optional LiPo battery and the USB-C port.

articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
articles.summary:
Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.

As food companies navigate increasingly complex product development and safety requirements, connected data and generative AI could help scientists make better-informed decisions, reduce manual work and identify potential risks earlier.

Supplier specifications are locked inside PDFs. Trial results sit in spreadsheets. Regulatory requirements arrive by email. Even a single ingredient can carry a different name in each document: “haldi” in one file, “turmeric” in another and “Curcuma longa” in a regulatory note. None of these files is wrong. The problem is that the information is scattered.
As a result, the developer spends more time searching, matching, and verifying data than working on the product itself. This has become common across food, beverage, and wellness R&D. Creating a product is no longer only about getting the taste and texture right. It is also about managing and connecting an ever-growing volume of data.
Why the data load keeps growing
Food product development is becoming more complex, and food safety sits at the centre of that complexity. articles.title: Petition seeks 10-minute maximum hold times for Canadian telcos
articles.summary:
Amid growing telecom wait times and rising frustration from Canadians, a new petition wants the government to establish customer service access standards like maximum hold times.
A House of Commons petition filed this month asks Parliament to tell the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) to “establish a clear, measurable and enforceable customer-service access standard for telecommunications providers.”
The petition also calls for establishing a “maximum 10-minute telephone hold time for customers seeking access to human customer service,” and asks the CRTC to determine how to measure hold times as well as to create “reasonable exceptions” to the rule.
Elsewhere, the petition says the customer service standards should require access to a human representative instead of connecting to automated systems. Specifically, the human representative should be able to start helping with the customer’s concern to prevent unnecessary transfers or further waiting.
Finally, and perhaps most crucially, the petition seeks the creation of “meaningful and proportional consequences for providers that persistently fail.”
At the time of writing, the petition had about 50 signatures. While not many, it’s worth noting the creator also made a similar Change.org petition that received nearly 1,200 signatures. The House of Commons petition closes on Nov. 26, 2026 at 1:03 p.m. ET.

Virtana lets its AI agents pull in agents from other vendors to work IT incidents
Information technology observability company Virtana today added Agentic Observability Enterprise Management to its platform so its artificial intelligence agents can pull agents from other vendors into an IT incident.
The release goes after a gap left by the way enterprises have adopted AI agents so far. Most enterprise agents have come built into a single vendor’s product, such as an IT service management system. When a failure spreads across systems from several vendors, none of those agents sees the whole outage. Collating the findings still falls to engineers.
With the new capabilities, a Virtana agent that spots trouble can invite other vendors’ agents into the investigation. Any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol or the open Agent2Agent protocol is eligible, including those bundled with software a company already owns.
Outside agents have been able to query Virtana’s monitoring data since February, when the company released its System-Aware MCP Server. The feed runs to more than 25,000 real-time metrics.
